title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
prompt:
Find the k-th largest value in an array (k-th largest in sorted order, so duplicates count separately). For example, the 2nd-highest reading score in a class.

Write kthLargest(nums, k). A finished MinHeap class is at the top of the editor; use it.

  • kthLargest([3, 2, 1, 5, 6, 4], 2) returns 5
  • kthLargest([3, 2, 3, 1, 2, 4, 5, 5, 6], 4) returns 4
  • kthLargest([7], 1) returns 7

Constraints: 1 <= k <= nums.length <= 105; values can be negative. Target: O(n log k) with a heap of size k. (Sorting is O(n log n) and would also pass; try the heap.)

tests.name: k = 1 is the max, k = n is the min
does not sort as strings
tests.code: assertEqual(kthLargest([100, 9, 20, 3], 2), 20, 'sort() without a comparator puts 100 before 20 and 9');

hints: Trigger: "k-th largest", "top k", "k closest" = a heap of size k. Counter-intuitive part: for the k largest, use a min-heap.
Push every number. Whenever the heap holds more than k items, pop the smallest. What survives is the k largest values, and the top of the heap (the smallest survivor) is the answer.

Shape:

const heap = new MinHeap();
for (const num of nums) {
  heap.push(num);
  if (heap.size() > k) heap.pop();
}
return heap.peek();
explain:
Time O(n log k): n pushes and pops on a heap that never exceeds k + 1 items. Space O(k). Sorting is O(n log n) time and simpler; for k = 2 and n = 100,000 the heap does roughly 100,000 × 1 steps versus 100,000 × 17 for the sort. The heap also works on a stream you can't hold in memory.

Say it: "Top-k, so a size-k min-heap: push each value, pop when it grows past k. The root is the k-th largest. O(n log k) time, O(k) space. If k is close to n or n is small, sorting is fine and simpler."
